phrases.t: I'd like to reserve a table for two.
phrases.ipa: /aɪd laɪk tə rɪˈzɜːrv ə ˈteɪbəl fər tuː/
phrases.tr: İki kişilik bir masa ayırtmak istiyorum.
phrases.tip: re-SERVE — land the beat on the second syllable.

phrases.t: Where can I pick up my boarding pass?
phrases.ipa: /wɛr kən aɪ pɪk ʌp maɪ ˈbɔːrdɪŋ pæs/
phrases.tip: BOARDing — compound nouns stress the first part.

phrases.t: How long does the flight take?
phrases.tip: The GH in flight is silent — just say FLITE.

phrases.t: Could you drop me off at the main entrance?
phrases.ipa: /kʊd ju drɑːp mi ɔf æt ðə meɪn ˈɛntrəns/
phrases.tip: Drop me OFF — the phrasal verb stress lands on off.

phrases.t: I have a reservation under the name Alex.
phrases.ipa: /aɪ hæv ə rɛzərˈveɪʃən ˈʌndər ðə neɪm ˈælɪks/
phrases.tip: reserVAtion — the third syllable carries the beat.
in-CLUDED — finish strong on the second word.
CHECK-out — first part of the compound wins.

phrases.t: I'd like a window seat, please.
phrases.tr: Cam kenarı bir koltuk istiyorum, lütfen.
phrases.tip: A crisp W — don't let it round into a V.
The T softens into CH — say PIK-chur.

phrases.t: Do you have a map of the city?
phrases.ipa: /du ju hæv ə mæp əv ðə ˈsɪti/
phrases.tip: CITY — the T flaps like a quick D in American English.

phrases.t: Let's touch base early next week.
phrases.tip: Touch BASE — the phrasal verb lands on base.
FOL-low — keep the final L soft and light.

phrases.t: Could we schedule a call for tomorrow?
phrases.ipa: /kʊd wi ˈskɛdʒuːl ə kɔl fər təˈmɑːroʊ/
phrases.tr: Yarın için bir görüşme ayarlayabilir miyiz?
phrases.tip: toMORrow — the second syllable wins.

phrases.t: I'm afraid I have a conflict at that time.
phrases.ipa: /aɪm əˈfreɪd aɪ hæv ə ˈkɑːnflɪkt æt ðæt taɪm/
phrases.tr: O saatte bir çakışmam var, korkarım.
phrases.tip: aFRAID — start soft, land on the second syllable.
THAT opens with the voiced TH — tongue between teeth.
CIR-cle — the R colors the whole first syllable.

phrases.t: I'll have the report ready by Friday.
phrases.ipa: /aɪl hæv ðə rɪˈpɔːrt ˈrɛdi baɪ ˈfraɪdeɪ/
phrases.tip: It's a rePORT — not a REport.

phrases.t: Could you clarify the last point?
phrases.tip: CLARE-ify — let the L flow through the cluster.
TIGHT ends in a crisp T — don't drop it.
THANKS — unvoiced TH, airy and light.
GOing shrinks to a soft ginning — HOWZ-it-GUN.

phrases.t: What do you do for a living?
phrases.ipa: /wʌt du ju du fər ə ˈlɪvɪŋ/
phrases.tip: The main DO carries the stress — what do you DO.

phrases.t: It was nice running into you.
phrases.tip: RUNning — double N, bounce the syllables.
CAN'T keeps its long A even when it's quick.

phrases.t: What have you been up to?
phrases.tip: Been can say bin — the American way.
COFfee — the first syllable is the hot one.
SOUNDS — let the final DZ ring.
BET-ter — the middle T flaps like a D.

phrases.t: Say hi to your family for me.
phrases.ipa: /seɪ haɪ tu jər ˈfæməli fər mi/
phrases.tip: FAMily — three light beats, first one strongest.
CATCHing — the T melts into a soft CH.
THEIR — keep the R soft at the end.
THORough — airy TH, tongue between teeth.

phrases.t: The weather in February is unpredictable.
phrases.tip: FEB-ru-air-ee — all four beats, with the first R.
parTICularly — find the TICK in the middle.
Colleague ends tight — KOL-eegz.

phrases.t: The development of vocabulary takes determination.
phrases.tip: voCABulary — the CAB carries the beat.
ik-SPER-uh-ment — the second syllable explodes.
proNUNciation — the NUN pops.
RES-tuh-ront — three beats, first one strong.

phrases.t: Wednesday is the sixth of November.
phrases.tip: Wednesday hides its first D — WENZ-day.

phrases.t: Thank you for having me today.
phrases.tip: HAVing — the -ing never takes the stress.
aDAPTability — DAPT is the drumbeat.

phrases.t: I have five years of experience in marketing.
phrases.ipa: /aɪ hæv faɪv jɪrz əv ɪkˈspɪriəns ɪn ˈmɑːrkɪtɪŋ/
phrases.tr: Pazarlama alanında beş yıllık deneyimim var.
phrases.tip: exPERience — three beats, second one lands.

phrases.t: I'm a quick learner and a team player.
phrases.ipa: /aɪm ə kwɪk ˈlɜːrnər ænd ə tim ˈpleɪər/
phrases.tip: QUICK LEARNer — punch the first word, glide the rest.

phrases.t: Could you tell me more about the role?
phrases.ipa: /kʊd ju tɛl mi mɔr əˈbaʊt ðə roʊl/
phrases.tr: Pozisyon hakkında biraz daha bilgi verebilir misiniz?
phrases.tip: Could you → COULD-ya — link the words.

phrases.t: I'd love the chance to contribute.
phrases.tip: conTRIbute — the TRI pops.

phrases.t: What does the day-to-day look like?
phrases.tip: DAY-to-day — the outside beats are the strong ones.
immeDIately — hold the middle beat.
GREAT — round the lips on the vowel.

phrases.t: I look forward to hearing from you.
phrases.ipa: /aɪ lʊk ˈfɔːrwərd tu ˈhɪrɪŋ frʌm ju/
phrases.tip: forWARD — the second syllable falls away.
TWENty — bite the lower lip for the W.
DIScount — first syllable wins.

phrases.t: The total comes to one hundred forty.
phrases.ipa: /ðə ˈtoʊtəl kʌmz tu wʌn ˈhʌndrərd ˈfɔːrti/
phrases.tip: HUNDred — both D's stay soft and quick.
CASH — the A stretches wide.
acCEPT — stress the second beat.
HALF price — the L softens almost away.

phrases.t: My number is five five five, zero two one nine.
phrases.ipa: /maɪ ˈnʌmbər ɪz faɪv faɪv faɪv ˈzɪroʊ tu wʌn naɪn/
phrases.tr: Numaram beş beş beş, sıfır iki bir dokuz.
phrases.tip: ZERO — keep the Z buzzing, not an H.

phrases.t: The meeting is at nine thirty.
phrases.tip: NINE THIRty — the TH stays airy.
TICKets — the plural S hisses.
exPENsive — the middle syllable pays.

phrases.t: I have a headache and a fever.
phrases.ipa: /aɪ hæv ə ˈhɛdeɪk ænd ə ˈfivər/
phrases.tip: HEADache — first beat strongest.

phrases.t: I need to see a doctor.
phrases.tip: NEED to — reduce the second word to ta.
PHARmacy — the PH says F.
alLERgic — middle beat lands.
HURTS — the final TS snaps.
AMbulance — three beats.

phrases.t: I've had this pain for three days.
phrases.ipa: /aɪv hæd ðɪs peɪn fər θri deɪz/
phrases.tip: PAIN — the diphthong glides down.
preSCRIPtion — the SCR cluster rolls.
DIZzy — buzz the Z twice.
SErious — two light beats.
NOW — let the vowel open wide.
You're ON mute — the middle word carries.
SHARE — the SH spreads the lips.
SEND you → SEN-cha — natural linking.
KEEPS — hold the final S.
offLINE — the phrasal stress flips to the end.
DOcument — first beat.

phrases.t: I have a hard stop at five.
phrases.ipa: /aɪ hæv ə hɑːrd stɑp æt faɪv/
phrases.tr: Beşte katılmam gereken bir şeyim var.
phrases.tip: HARD stop — both words punch.
BREAking — the long A glides.
STANDup — compound stress up front.
